chunks: Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who is in the ship and does not know where the Qiblah is, he said: He should strive to determine it, but if he does not know, he prays facing its head (front).
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim perform prayer on a ship if they cannot determine the Qiblah direction?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *ijtihād* (diligent effort) in determining the Qiblah for travelers on vessels, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams regarding mobility and uncertainty. It underscores the Shia legal maxim that when precise orientation is impossible, one prays in the direction of their best estimate, ensuring the validity of the prayer despite environmental constraints. This ruling highlights the flexibility within Shia fiqh to accommodate the realities of travel without compromising religious obligation.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the man who happens to be in the ship, so he does not know where the Qiblah is’. Heasws said: ‘He should investigate, but if he does not know, he can pray Salāt around its head (front part)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in a ship and does not know the direction of al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah).
He (the Imam) said, ‘He must make an effort to find the direction al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah) and if he cannot find it, performs Salah (prayer) facing toward where its head is.’”
